title: Bunk's buoyant style, one-handed playing and showmanship
summary: Blumberg describes his precise bouncy style; they recall Bunk playing with one hand while leafing through music and his sense of showmanship.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah, well, he'd hit notes like he'd crack a whip. It was just beautiful precision and cleanliness about his playing. And he played a very buoyant style, kind of bouncy, I guess you'd call it. I don't know. It's pretty hard to really... Yeah, I know it's hard to describe any style. Just put it all into words.
Is there anything else about the way he'd sit around? I noticed he'd always sit like he was quite relaxed.

Yeah. Yeah, I remember sometimes... Well, he was always leafing through his music. He had a big stack of lead sheets up there of all these different tunes. And he'd be sitting there sometimes playing, holding the horn up with one hand. And it didn't make any difference to him whether it was the right hand or the left hand. He'd just... Sometimes he'd play through a couple choruses with his left hand, holding the horn and fingering it with the left hand, which isn't an exceptionally difficult thing. But it didn't seem to bother... He didn't even seem to be aware of it, you know. And he'd be leafing through the music with his right hand and reaching around for things.

I can remember one night. That's about the second or third week the band first opened there. And the Metronome editor, Simon, or whoever his name was, went to Leonard Feather. And there's two or three other people from Metronome, I think, were there. Not Feather, but some other people. And Bunk sort of put on an act for him. He'd play with one hand. I guess his right hand. He'd hold the horn with the right hand and the finger. And he'd be buttoning his coat.
He was always doing things like that. So he could play with one hand.
He'd be buttoning his coat and fixing his handkerchief or something in a pocket. And always busy with that other hand doing things to show.
So some of that was an act, too. Yeah, sure.
Although ordinarily he didn't care anything about showmanship, as you know. It was strictly the music.
Yeah. Except that in his way, he was a fine showman. Yeah, that's right. He consistently presented a very exciting image to go along with the playing. Yeah. A lean, very lean fella. And...
Yeah, and before the band opened, for instance, he asked to get the music stands all fixed up with the names painted on and little crowns painted on.
I mean, it wasn't that he just didn't care how the looks. I don't mean that. The music, of course, was a big thing with him, naturally. That's right.
